{{short description|College football season}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}} {{Use American English|date=February 2026}} {{Infobox college sports team season | sport = football | year = 1969 | team = Doane Tigers | image = | image_size = | conference = [[Great Plains Athletic Conference|Nebraska Intercollegiate Athletic Conference]] | short_conf = NIAC | record = 8–0 | conf_record = 5–0 | head_coach = [[Al Papik]] | hc_year = 15th | captain = Dick Held | captain2 = Larry Green | captain3 = Paul Schelstraete | stadium = Simon Field | champion = NIAC champion }} {{1969 Nebraska Intercollegiate Athletic Conference football standings}} The '''1969 Doane Tigers football team''' was an [[American football]] team that represented [[Doane University]] as a member of the [[Great Plains Athletic Conference|Nebraska Intercollegiate Athletic Conference]] (NIAC) during the [[1969 NAIA football season]]. In their 15th year under head coach [[Al Papik]], the team compiled an 8–0 record (5–0 against NIAC opponents), won the NIAC championship, and outscored opponents by a total of 272 to 95. Doane was ranked No. 11 in the final NAIA rankings in late November. The 1969 season was the fourth of four consecutive undefeated seasons and part of a 38-game undefeated streak that began with the last two games of the 1965 season and continued until September 19, 1970.{{cite news|title=A Small School, but You Can Learn To Hate It|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=October 13, 1969|url=https://vault.si.com/vault/1969/10/13/a-small-school-but-you-can-learn-to-hate-it}}{{cite web|title=A win for the ages: ending the nation's longest unbeaten streak|author=Jacob Knabel|date=June 8, 2016|publisher=Concordia University Nebraska (reprinted from Football)|url=https://www.cune.edu/athletics/teams/football/news/win-ages-ending-nations-longest-win-streak}} In October 1969, ''Sports Illustrated'' published a feature story on the rise of Doane football, noting,
That Doane, with an enrollment of 738 (492 boys), should become a football power is as surprising as if Ohio State gave up the game. The school itself was founded 97 years ago and, though it started playing football in 1895, never, never before has there been anything like this.
Doane tailback Mike Sallier rushed for 1,054 yards on 229 carries, averaged 131.77 rushing yards per game, and scored 96 points in eight games.{{cite news|title=Doane Star Loses Lead|newspaper=Omaha World-Herald|date=November 15, 1969|page=17|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/omaha-world-herald-sallier/140454904/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}{{cite news|title=Sallier Ranked 4th In Scoring|newspaper=The Lincoln Star|date=November 22, 1969|page=14|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-lincoln-star-sallier-ranked-4th/140455319/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Doane quarterback Larry Green ranked among the NAIA leaders with 1,054 passing yards, an average of 195.7 yards per game. Larry Green, Dick Held, and Paul Schelstraete were the team captains. Held, a senior linebacker, wrote a weekly column in the school newspaper chronicling the season.{{cite news|title=Looking Back|newspaper=The Doane Owl|date=September 16,
